definitions.explanation: A visual or sensory perception that does not correspond to reality.
An incorrect understanding or belief about something.

examples.japanese: これは{目|め}の{錯覚|さっかく}だ。
{自分|じぶん}は{特別|とくべつ}だと{錯覚|さっかく}していた。
examples.english: I was under the illusion that I was special.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}が{早|はや}く{過|す}ぎたように{錯覚|さっかく}する。
examples.english: It feels like time passed quickly (but it didn't).

notes:
VERB FORM:
{錯覚|さっかく}する (to be under an illusion, to misperceive)

TYPES:
・{目|め}の{錯覚|さっかく} (optical illusion)
・{視覚|しかく}{錯覚|さっかく} (visual illusion)
・{聴覚|ちょうかく}{錯覚|さっかく} (auditory illusion)

USAGE:
・〜と{錯覚|さっかく}する (to mistakenly believe that ~)
・{錯覚|さっかく}を{起|お}こす (to create an illusion)
・{錯覚|さっかく}に{陥|おちい}る (to fall into a misperception)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{幻覚|げんかく} - hallucination (seeing things that aren't there)
・{幻想|げんそう} - illusion, fantasy (more abstract/romantic)
・{妄想|もうそう} - delusion, wild fantasy
・{思|おも}い{込|こ}み - assumption, jumping to conclusions
